sport_summary: 14-game Monday slate spans NBA, MLB, and NHL with playoff action plus a full MLB evening card

picks.reasoning: BetRivers is offering +140 on the Guardians -1.5 run line versus a median of +126 across the market — a massive 258 bps of edge, the highest spread edge on the entire slate. Joey Cantillo gets the ball for Cleveland against a struggling Angels offense, and the Guardians are favored at -164 to -175 on the moneyline, implying a high win probability that makes the run line a strong value at plus-money. Getting a team this heavily favored at +140 to cover -1.5 represents a genuine pricing inefficiency.

MyBookie posts +112 on the Yankees -1.5 run line, well above the median of +101 across 9 books — 258 bps of edge mirrors the top spread value on today's slate. The Yankees are priced as clear moneyline favorites (-148 to -167), and Ryan Weathers gets the start against Brandon Young for Baltimore, a matchup that favors New York's lineup depth. Plus-money on a heavy favorite's run line is exactly the kind of mispricing worth targeting.

BetMGM offers +125 on the Mariners -1.5 against a median of +119 — 122 bps of edge on a side where Seattle is a solid -135 to -146 moneyline favorite. George Kirby takes the mound for Seattle, one of the better starters in the AL, against Peter Lambert for Houston, a clear pitching mismatch. The Mariners being priced this short on the moneyline while the run line still returns plus-money at a premium book creates real value.

BetMGM's -102 on the Under 7.5 is the best price available versus a median of -109 across 9 books — 166 bps of edge on a total where the market is largely aligned around a low number. Michael Soroka starts for Arizona and Nathan Eovaldi for Texas, a pairing of groundball-oriented pitchers who both suppress hard contact and limit walks, keeping scores tight. Getting Under 7.5 at near even-money with two control pitchers projected is excellent value.

BetOnline.ag posts +189 on the Avalanche puck line versus a median of +176 across 9 books — 163 bps of edge at a very attractive plus-money price. Colorado is a -134 moneyline favorite, meaning they win outright more than half the time, and at +189 the implied probability on the puck line is only around 35%, making this a positive-EV proposition given their win probability. The NHL puck line historically provides value on road favorites priced in this range when the market underprices their win-by-two frequency.
